title: R6 production database migration and rollback rehearsal

law_conformance.note: The frozen TypeScript engine has no typed rehearsal journal, canonical rollback receipt, or migration eligibility handoff. This corpus therefore states the ratified R6 contract and names no invented oracle capture.

preserves: Existing database domain rows survive the selected Rust migration exactly.
The production source is opened read-only; mutation occurs only in disposable snapshots.
Source, candidate, backup, and rollback trust is bound to distinct retained physical file identities.
A verified pre-mutation backup restores into a new database and is compared exactly.
Every durable phase is immutable, hash-linked, bounded, and restartable.
intentionally_excludes: No daily-driver database is opened writable.
No dual-write mode and no TypeScript migration implementation are retained.
Service election, retirement, registration mutation, and cutover commit remain exclusively owned by the unified R6 release authority.

determinism.clock: All rehearsal instants come from an injected fixed ClockAuthority.
determinism.identifiers: Run and migration identifiers are literal action-owned values.
determinism.filesystem: Each replay uses a bounded disposable temporary root and removes only that exact root.

record_contracts.actions: Ordinals are contiguous. rehearse creates the backup-first candidate and eligibility handoff, resume repeats the same run, restore creates a new rollback artifact, and backup-absent proves a checkpoint cannot synthesize missing evidence.
record_contracts.durable: One exact outcome row is produced for each action; refusal rows are observations and never hidden skips.
record_contracts.state: The fold records admitted/refused counts, handoff readiness, and source-byte preservation.

evidence.claim: Parses every action, executes it through public release APIs, and compares the produced durable and state projections byte-for-value.
Deletes each suffix of the immutable checkpoint chain while leaving effects ahead and requires exact successful recovery.
Makes the candidate a hard link of the source and proves refusal occurs before checkpoint residue or source mutation.
Replaces the candidate with a source hard link after initial checks and proves retained identity revalidation refuses at the write boundary.
Invokes the removed cutover command with fabricated retirement data and proves fixed refusal without registration mutation.
Proves the typed handoff contains database eligibility evidence and no retirement, election, registration, or commit authority fields.
Compares revision, ordered sources, supersession matrix, and release receipt exactly against the staged current law pack.
Ignored evidence-machine witness migrates and restores the sanitized 406 MiB clone while proving source bytes unchanged.
